name: recutils
desc: Tools to work with human-editable, plain text data files
why: GNU recutils treats plain text files as typed databases with a query language, an unusual and underused take on data.

brief.what_it_is: GNU Recutils is a set of tools and libraries for working with human-editable, plain text databases called recfiles. A recfile holds a sequence of records, and each record has any number of named fields. Its features include typed fields (predefined types such as integer, real and date, plus user-defined types based on regular expressions), constraints such as mandatory and unique fields, joins, grouping, sorting and aggregate functions, and password-based AES encryption of individual fields. It ships converters for mdb and CSV files, report templates, and editor support for Vim and Emacs. The executables in the package are csv2rec, rec2csv, recdel, recfix, recfmt, recinf, recins, recsel and recset.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents recfiles as plain-text databases that people can edit by hand, with the structure and checks of a typed database. The README does not state a longer motivation in its own words.
brief.how_it_works: Data lives in ordinary text files as records made of named fields, so any text editor can change it. The rec* utilities and the librec C library read and write these files, and the type system and constraints are enforced on that data. The homepage does not describe the internal mechanism in more detail.
brief.install_notes: Binary packages are listed for Trisquel, Fedora, openSUSE, Debian, Arch, Mandrake, Parabola, OpenCSW for Solaris, FreeBSD, Termux for Android and Void Linux. Source tarballs come from the GNU FTP server and its mirrors. The rec-mode Emacs mode is distributed through ELPA. The homepage does not give specific build steps or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: Most database tools want a server or a binary store, but this one keeps the data as plain text that a person can edit in any editor and still gives it typed fields, constraints, joins and aggregates. Field-level encryption inside a text file is also unusual.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage was updated 2025/03/26, the manual was last updated September 23, 2024, and the README names an active maintainer, Jose E. Marchesi, who is reachable through the mailing lists. I did not find a release version or release date on the pages I read.
brief.caveats: The brew formula has no caveats. The pages I read contain no command examples, so I could not check usage from them. The homepage refers to IRC on freenode, which may be out of date. The manual is an index of download formats and does not show the content of the manual itself. The FSF page is licensed CC BY-ND, but the software is GPL-3.0-or-later.
quotes: GNU Recutils is a set of tools and libraries to access human-editable, plain text databases called recfiles.
The data is stored as a sequence of records, each record containing an arbitrary number of named fields.
